correctness.rationale: For n>=5 independent unit-rate exponential circular gaps E_i and T=sum E_i, Dirichlet normalization makes the reciprocal-pair count R=sum 1{E_i < E_(i-1), E_i < E_(i+1)} and directed length L=(sum min(E_(i-1),E_i))/T. T is independent of both R and L. The four nonzero indicator/minimum overlap covariances per i are two -1/18 and two +1/24; other pairs use disjoint exponentials, giving Cov(R,Q)=-n/36 and Cov(R,L)=-1/36. Adjacent local minima are mutually exclusive and distance-two joint probability 2/15, yielding VarR=2n/45. Each minimum of two exponentials has mean 1/2, variance 1/4, adjacent minimum covariance 1/12; using T Gamma(n,1) yields EL=1/2 and VarL=1/[6(n+1)]. These imply the claimed correlation -sqrt(15)/12 * sqrt((n+1)/n). Independent exact rational gap-order enumeration over all 5!,6!,7!,8! permutations checks all moments, not extrapolated as proof.
residual_risks: n>=5 is essential to ensure four local B_j overlaps have distinct cyclic indices; directed, not undirected, length convention, intrinsic circular geodesic distance, no ties, iid uniform sample only.

originality.rationale: Reflexive/mutual pair counts, weak component counts, and local minima are aliases; Bahadır–Ceyhan give separate reciprocal-count moments for interval samples. Penrose–Wade give total nearest-neighbor length results on intervals and online graph processes. Wilsher–Dettmann–Ganesh examine a probabilistic soft-geometric graph on a circle, not deterministic nearest neighbor links. Even exact knowledge of both marginal laws does not determine the mixed covariance. A fresh Resultary query did not surface this exact joint observable, though a broader stabilization covariance theorem or older stochastic geometry tables remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: An older geometric probability theorem might contain a joint count-length covariance implicitly, possibly in an interval-to-circle specialization.
